page: Amazon Web Services m7a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 3077.37 and a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 13.81 GB/sec. Multi-core performance and general integer operations fall within the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6089.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 10567.1. However, a notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks, where both read and write speeds register in the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Conversely, cached small-block memory reads remain average at 585.94 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the m7a.xlarge delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of local storage. The instance is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis key-value stores processing up to 10.51 million SET operations per second, and light text processing tasks.
